_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Reading your route and the weather…

description: Weather and a flyover for a GPX file or route the user shares. If the user attached a GPX or route file, call plan_route and pass the file as gpx_file; if you can read the file's contents yourself, you may instead pass its text as gpx or its points as points. Never treat a file name as an event name. Also a Ride with GPS or GPX link, or another app's route points: the weather along it at the time they'd ride or run it, and a flyover of the route (a flyby, fly over my route) that plays in the chat, coloured by the weather: the forecast within 10 days, 10 years of weather on that date beyond it, rated by Windline's forecast engine, with the headwind and tailwind stretches, heat and rain. No account needed. For "What will the wind be like on this route on Saturday at 6?" or "Show me the weather for this GPX and a flyover". The route stays theirs: nothing is published. For a 3D flight and a route video, offer to save it as a private ride or run with create_event (visibility private). Several GPX files are one multi-day tour: pass them all as files (ordered by the numbers in their names, else by the map; one day after another from start), never one call per file. A route can also come from another app's tool as its points or an encoded polyline (for example a route or activity map from a fitness app): pass it as polyline or points. Never ask the user to export a GPX if you already have the route's points.

files.description: Several GPX files (a multi-day tour): ordered by the numbers in their names, else by the map; one day after another from start.

items.description: A GPX file (its text, or a link to it) or a route's polyline or points, and its name (the name helps order the days).

download_url.description: ChatGPT: the attached file's download link.

points.description: The day as its points, [[lat, lon], …].

polyline.description: The day as an encoded polyline (another app's route or activity map).

url.description: A link to the GPX or route (Ride with GPS; not Strava).

gpx.description: The GPX file's text (up to 5 MB): if the user pasted it, or attached a file you can read yourself (for example with code).

gpx_file.description: The GPX or route file the user attached (ChatGPT passes it here).

file_name.description: Its name, if known (the route's name; never an event's).

gpx_files.description: Several GPX or route files the user attached (ChatGPT passes them here): one per day of a tour, ordered by the numbers in their names, else by the map.

items.description: One attached GPX or route file.

file_name.description: Its name, if known (the route's name; never an event's).

name.description: What to call the plan, if the user named it.

pace.description: Riding speed in km/h (default 25), or running pace in minutes per km (default 6).

points.description: The route as its points: [[lat, lon], …], with elevation in metres as a third number if known. Up to 50,000. Use it for points another app's tool gave, or that you read from an attached file (GPX, FIT, TCX) with code.

polyline.description: The route as an encoded polyline (Google's format, precision 5 or 6), as another app's tool gives it (a route's or an activity's map).

rest_days.description: With files: dates with no riding, "YYYY-MM-DD", only if the user named rest days.

start.description: When they start, "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" local to the route. Ask if they didn't say.

starts.description: Each day's own local start, "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", when they differ.

tz.description: The route's IANA time zone, if known (else worked out from where it starts).

units.description: Pass the asker's units: imperial for users in the US, UK road distances, Liberia or Myanmar, or when they ask in miles/°F; otherwise metric.

url.description: A link to the route: a Ride with GPS route, ride or collection (a collection gives one day per route), or any public link to a GPX file. Not Strava.

name: plan_route

outputSchema.description: The weather along a route at the time you'd ride or run it.

basis.description: forecast (Apple Weather, within 10 days), historic (10 years of Copernicus ERA5 on that date) or mixed.

days.description: Each day: name, date (ISO), basis, rating (good, fair, tough), why, start_temp_c, finish_temp_c, effort_pct (cycling), heat_stress and wbgt_c (running), rain_mm or rain_days_in_10 and usual_high_c.

error.description: When the call failed: what went wrong, in words for the user.

events.description: Several events matched: their names. Ask the user which one.

files.description: Several files: the file of each day, in order.

fly_3d.description: A link to the full 3D flight, only for a route with a public page; else null.

flyover.description: The map flies over the route in the chat.

message.description: When view is "none": what to tell the user (no match, not live yet, a question back).

order.description: Several files: how the days were ordered (numbers, map or upload).

order_note.description: When the file numbers and the map disagree: what was chosen.

signup.description: Without a sign-in: { label, url } to make a free Windline or RunFast account (?ref=mcp).

sponsor_line.description: The line every answer ends with: who brings livedot's live tracking free.

timed_for.description: What the times assume (the start, the pace).

view.description: What this answer is; "none" when there is nothing to show (see message).

title: Weather along your route
